adopted: The list is a grammar, so a head-only payload is not a message
consequences: The two artefacts diverged here and the corpus could not see it: the specification never required a body, the reference required one for any non-empty payload, and every vector stayed green because none carries a head section without a body.
msg-neg-head-without-body is the isolating vector, refused under this reading and admitted under the other, so the divergence becomes a verdict rather than a note.
The zero-octet case keeps its own vector, whose note already records it as a reading: a payload of no octets is admitted as a message with no sections, under either reading of this question.
evidence: The messaging artifact presents the bare message as a sequence: zero or one of each head section, then "The body consists of one of the following three choices: one or more data sections, one or more amqp-sequence sections, or a single amqp-value section", then zero or one footer. It names no condition for a payload that carries a head and nothing else, so the question is how that sequence is read rather than what it says.
question: Must a payload that carries any section carry a body, or does the body list only constrain which section kinds may appear as one?

readings.name: The list is a grammar, so a head-only payload is not a message
readings.statement: Adopted. The list is presented as a sequence — head, body, tail — and reading the body clause as a constraint on kinds rather than as an element of that sequence leaves the sequence with a hole only that reading needs. A payload carrying a header and nothing else is therefore not a message and is refused, while the zero-octet payload stays admitted because a transfer with no payload carries no message at all, which is a different thing from a message missing its body.

readings.name: The body list constrains only the kinds that may appear as a body, so a head-only payload is admitted
readings.statement: Rejected. Defensible on the text taken as a list of permitted sections rather than as a sequence, and it admits a message with no body, which no clause describes and no peer is known to send.
